assignments.reason: The Tzaddik's close followers (אֲנָשָׁיו הַמְקֹרָבִין אֵלָיו) are described in the source text as 'אַנְשֵׁי מַעֲשֶׂה יְרֵאִים וּשְׁלֵמִים' — people of action, God-fearing and whole. Their essential nature is an extension of the Tzaddik's holiness: they are the human impression of his seal, the wax that reveals his hidden letters. They belong to the domain of the Tzaddik and the seal by nature, not merely by causal proximity.

Understanding the Tzaddik's greatness (מַעֲלַת הַצַּדִּיק) is essentially knowledge of the Tzaddik himself — it is the readable impression that the seal leaves. Its essential nature belongs entirely to the domain of the Tzaddik and his knowability. The Torah's entire argument is about how the Tzaddik's stature, though beyond direct comprehension, can be grasped through his imprint. This concept is inseparable from the Tzaddik-seal domain.
